layers.label: Languages & runtimes
layers.decision: Keep the current language as the control. TypeScript/Node, Rust and .NET cover different host and deployment needs; compare rewrites only on a complete application journey.
layers.gate: Preserve outputs, diagnostics, ABI/FFI behavior, cold start, memory bounds and supported packaging; include migration and maintenance cost.

layers.label: Shared core & native boundaries
layers.decision: Separate portable domain contracts from host capabilities. The TypeScript compiler supports a shared implementation; its compiler tests do not establish cross-host behavior. CXX, WASI and worker bridges address different boundaries.
layers.gate: Run one contract corpus through every required host; verify error transport, cancellation, ownership, schema evolution and total serialization/IPC cost.

layers.label: Browser extensions
layers.decision: Use the browser lifecycle and native-messaging protocol as the reference constraints; compare build and UI tools without depending on a permanently alive worker.
layers.gate: Survive worker termination, permission changes, reconnects and version skew while preserving durable state and strict message validation.

layers.label: Desktop shells & native UI
layers.decision: Compare a complete installed desktop slice. Electron is a web-runtime control; WinUI is a Windows-native control. Native/webview alternatives need the same platform features.
layers.gate: Match rich media, accessibility, IME, drag/drop, high DPI, native IPC, install/update behavior and target OS coverage before ranking latency or memory.

layers.label: Large collections & interaction
layers.decision: Keep the complete data model while virtualizing presentation. Hold the UI framework fixed when comparing virtualization; TanStack Virtual can complement React. Compare framework changes through the full interaction workload.
layers.gate: Preserve every item, order, selection, focus, search, accessibility and live update during scrolling; measure input/scroll tails and memory with real media.

layers.label: Games, graphics & physics
layers.decision: Choose an engine, renderer or physics library within its actual role. Separate native/browser exports and visual settings; advanced rendering papers are research lanes.
layers.gate: Pass identical visual, input, audio, persistence and asset checks; then compare frame tails, load time and resource use on declared devices.

layers.label: Assets, textures & delivery
layers.decision: Use a reproducible authoring/export baseline; compare mesh, glTF and texture transformations independently before combining them.
layers.gate: Preserve geometry, animation, materials, color, metadata and licensing; compare transfer, decode/upload time, GPU memory and perceptual error together.

layers.label: Mod loaders & compatibility
layers.decision: The exact game, loader, runtime and modpack determine eligibility. Fabric, NeoForge and BepInEx are ecosystem-specific controls, not interchangeable ranked replacements.
layers.gate: Run the pinned game/loader/mod corpus through install, dependency/load order, conflict diagnostics, startup, update and uninstall; preserve saves and user files.

layers.label: Plugins & process isolation
layers.decision: Choose a boundary that contains the actual untrusted workload: WebAssembly components, OS process isolation and embedded scripts have different host capability contracts.
layers.gate: Test forbidden filesystem/network/process access, resource exhaustion, cancellation and escape attempts; document the trusted host API and per-OS restrictions.

layers.label: Dependencies & conflict solving
layers.decision: Compare solvers on one explicit version, feature, conflict and preference model. A legal and explainable installation plan is the outcome.
layers.gate: Use satisfiable and unsatisfiable corpora with a small exhaustive oracle; require deterministic plans, complete conflicts and bounded cancellation.

layers.label: Files, hashing & archives
layers.decision: Measure the entire inventory/extract/hash operation. Traversal, change detection, hashing, chunking and archive tools are separate variables with a complete-scan control.
layers.gate: Keep hidden/ignored files when required, path and link policies, malformed-input errors, output hashes and cancellation; measure cold I/O, memory and recovery.

layers.label: Local storage & search
layers.decision: Start with durable relational metadata and lexical search; introduce specialized KV or vector stores only when the query/workload justifies their contract.
layers.gate: Match transactions, committed records, full search relevance, filters, update visibility and crash recovery under a fixed memory/storage allowance.

layers.label: Downloads, transfer & sync
layers.decision: Use verified HTTP transfers as the control. Compare range/delta or peer transfer only with the same trusted identity, complete content and recovery policy.
layers.gate: Reject changed validators and corrupt chunks; handle ignored ranges, disconnects, retries, cancellation and source mutation without mixing versions.

layers.label: APIs & shared services
layers.decision: Keep API semantics and deployment budgets fixed. Language/runtime and framework changes are distinct variables; shared service storage is a separate cohort from embedded storage.
layers.gate: Preserve validation, auth boundaries, errors, consistency, timeouts and load behavior; report tail latency, useful throughput and full operational cost.

layers.label: Signed distribution & updates
layers.decision: Combine versioned update metadata, artifact identity, provenance and platform installation deliberately. A signature alone does not provide rollback/freeze protection or atomic installation.
layers.gate: Reject expired, replayed, wrong-signer and mismatched artifacts; test rotation, delegation, interrupted updates, downgrade policy and restoration of user data.

layers.label: Builds & reproducibility
layers.decision: Compare a pinned current build with incremental, hermetic or reproducibility tooling. Keep clean, warmed and changed-input builds in separate lanes.
layers.gate: Preserve emitted artifacts, diagnostics and dependency integrity; verify environment locks, cache invalidation, binary differences and CI portability.

layers.label: Testing, profiling & correctness
layers.decision: Use end-to-end tests and saved traces as controls. Add replay, fuzzing and model exploration for explicit fault classes; each tool has its own coverage limits.
layers.gate: Retain seeded faults, false positives, missed defects, trace loss, instrumentation overhead and replay limits; a clean run is not a proof of correctness.

layers.label: Optional AI & developer tools
layers.decision: Treat AI as an optional feature or engineering tool with a declared task and budget. Compare full model/runtime/agent configurations rather than framework names alone.
layers.gate: Require useful held-out task quality, privacy/tool boundaries, completed outputs, cost and latency budgets; keep publisher scores separate from local reproduction.

layers.label: Background work & recovery
layers.decision: Choose a local journal or service workflow to fit the deployment boundary. Do not introduce a remote orchestrator merely to run a desktop job.
layers.gate: Recover from crashes at every state transition with explicit idempotency, retry, cancellation and external side-effect rules; retain acknowledged work and full diagnostics.

layers.label: Analytics & result formats
layers.decision: Use the same complete benchmark/telemetry dataset and query semantics. Compare engines and storage formats as separate variables.
layers.gate: Preserve values, nulls, ordering and full aggregates; require completion beyond RAM with fixed resource limits and retained spill/error evidence.
